packet.headline_seed: Meta buys robotic startup to bolster its humanoid AI ambitions
packet.description_seed: Meta bought humanoid startup Assured Robot Intelligence to beef up its AI models for robots, the company said.

what: Meta buys robotic startup to bolster its humanoid AI ambitions

clean_source_blocks.text: Meta bought humanoid startup Assured Robot Intelligence to beef up its AI models for robots, the company said.

Meta acquired Assured Robot Intelligence, a startup co-founded by former Fauna Robotics co-founder Lerrel Pinto and former Nvidia researcher Xiaolong Wang, to bolster its humanoid robotics platform strategy. The deal, which brings whole-body robot control models and tactile sensor technology into Meta Superintelligence Labs, reveals Meta’s ambition to be the Android of humanoids: provide the intelligence layer and let others build the machines.

Lerrel Pinto co-founded Fauna Robotics, a startup that built an approachable bipedal robot called Sprout. He left in 2025. Amazon acquired Fauna in March, along with its 50 employees and its $50,000, three-and-a-half-foot-tall dancing humanoid, to enter the consumer robotics market. Pinto then co-founded Assured Robot Intelligence with Xiaolong Wang, a former Nvidia researcher and associate professor at UC San Diego who won the MLSys 2024 Best Paper Award for work on AI model optimisation. On Friday, Meta acquired ARI and both founders joined Meta Superintelligence Labs. The acquisition closed the same day it was announced. Financial terms were not disclosed. The interesting question is not what Meta paid for a startup whose employees were concentrated in San Diego and New York. It is what Meta intends to do with the technology, and what that intention reveals about the company’s theory of how the humanoid market will develop.

Meta’s stated goal for robotics is to replicate what Google’s Android operating system and Qualcomm’s chips did for the smartphone industry: build the foundation that everyone else builds on. The company launched Meta Robotics Studio last year, hired former Cruise CEO Marc Whitten to lead the effort, and began recruiting roughly 100 engineers to develop in-house humanoid hardware alongside the AI models that power it. CTO Andrew Bosworth has described humanoid robots as Meta’s next bet of comparable scale to augmented reality, a category in which Meta has already spent tens of billions through its Reality Labs division. The ARI acquisition adds a specific capability to this effort: robot control models that enable humanoids to understand, predict, and adapt to human behaviour in unstructured environments.

payload.title: Meta osti robotiikkayhtiön vahvistaakseen humanoidirobottien tekoälyä
payload.summary: Meta on ostanut Assured Robot Intelligence -startupin vahvistaakseen humanoidirobotteihin liittyviä tekoälymallejaan. Kaupan taloudellisia ehtoja ei kerrottu.
payload.content:
Meta on ostanut Assured Robot Intelligence -nimisen robotiikkastartupin vahvistaakseen humanoidirobotteihin liittyviä tekoälymallejaan. Yhtiön mukaan hankinta tuo Meta Superintelligence Labsiin osaamista muun muassa koko kehon robottiohjauksen malleista ja tuntopalautteeseen liittyvästä anturiteknologiasta.

## Perustajat siirtyivät Metalle

Assured Robot Intelligencen perustivat Lerrel Pinto ja Xiaolong Wang. Pinto oli aiemmin mukana perustamassa Fauna Roboticsia, joka kehitti Sprout-nimistä kaksijalkaista robottia. Hän jätti Faunan vuonna 2025.

Wang on entinen Nvidian tutkija ja UC San Diegon apulaisprofessori. Aineiston mukaan hän sai MLSys 2024 Best Paper Award -palkinnon tekoälymallien optimointiin liittyvästä työstä.

Meta osti Assured Robot Intelligencen perjantaina, ja molemmat perustajat liittyivät Meta Superintelligence Labsiin. Kauppa sulkeutui samana päivänä kuin se julkistettiin. Taloudellisia ehtoja ei kerrottu.

## Meta hakee robotiikkaan alustaroolia

Aineiston mukaan Metan robotiikkatavoite muistuttaa sitä, mitä Android-käyttöjärjestelmä ja Qualcommin sirut ovat merkinneet älypuhelinalalle. Tavoitteena on rakentaa perusta, jonka varaan muut voivat kehittää omia laitteitaan.

Tulkinnan mukaan Meta haluaa olla humanoidirobottien niin sanottu älykerros: se tarjoaisi robotteihin ohjelmiston ja tekoälyn, kun taas muut valmistajat voisivat rakentaa fyysiset koneet.

Meta on jo perustanut Meta Robotics Studion ja palkannut entisen Cruise-johtajan Marc Whittenin vetämään hanketta. Lisäksi yhtiö on alkanut rekrytoida noin sataa insinööriä kehittämään sekä humanoidilaitteistoa että sitä käyttäviä tekoälymalleja.

## Painopisteenä robottien ohjaus ja ympäristöön sopeutuminen

Assured Robot Intelligencen hankinta lisää Metan robotiikkahankkeeseen erityisesti robottien ohjausmalleihin liittyvää osaamista. Aineiston mukaan kyse on malleista, joiden avulla humanoidirobotit voivat ymmärtää, ennakoida ja mukautua ihmisten käyttäytymiseen jäsentymättömissä ympäristöissä.

Teknologiaan liittyy myös tuntopalautteeseen perustuvaa anturiosaamista. Nämä ovat keskeisiä alueita, jos humanoidirobottien halutaan toimivan muuallakin kuin tarkasti rajatuissa laboratorio- tai tehdasympäristöissä.

Metan teknologiajohtaja Andrew Bosworth on kuvannut humanoidirobotteja yhtiön seuraavaksi suureksi panostukseksi lisätyn todellisuuden kokoluokassa. Meta on käyttänyt lisättyyn todellisuuteen ja Reality Labs -toimintoihin jo kymmeniä miljardeja dollareita.
summary_bullets: Perustajat Lerrel Pinto ja Xiaolong Wang siirtyivät Meta Superintelligence Labsiin.
payload.journalist_note: Artikkeli perustuu paketin tietoihin Metan Assured Robot Intelligence -kaupasta, perustajista, Meta Superintelligence Labsiin siirtymisestä, kaupan julkistus- ja sulkeutumispäivästä, julkistamattomista taloudellisista ehdoista sekä Metan robotiikkastrategiasta. Kauppahintaa, tarkkaa tuoteaikataulua tai Metan tulevia robottimalleja ei lisätty, koska niitä ei ollut aineistossa.

[Lähde: The Next Web]
Meta acquired Assured Robot Intelligence, a startup co-founded by former Fauna Robotics co-founder Lerrel Pinto and former Nvidia researcher Xiaolong Wang, to bolster its humanoid robotics platform strategy. The deal, which brings whole-body robot control models and tactile sensor technology into Meta Superintelligence Labs, reveals Meta’s ambition to be the Android of humanoids: provide the intelligence layer and let others build the machines.

Lerrel Pinto co-founded Fauna Robotics, a startup that built an approachable bipedal robot called Sprout. He left in 2025. Amazon acquired Fauna in March, along with its 50 employees and its $50,000, three-and-a-half-foot-tall dancing humanoid, to enter the consumer robotics market. Pinto then co-founded Assured Robot Intelligence with Xiaolong Wang, a former Nvidia researcher and associate professor at UC San Diego who won the MLSys 2024 Best Paper Award for work on AI model optimisation. On Friday, Meta acquired ARI and both founders joined Meta Superintelligence Labs. The acquisition closed the same day it was announced. Financial terms were not disclosed. The interesting question is not what Meta paid for a startup whose employees were concentrated in San Diego and New York. It is what Meta intends to do with the technology, and what that intention reveals about the company’s theory of how the humanoid market will develop.

Meta’s stated goal for robotics is to replicate what Google’s Android operating system and Qualcomm’s chips did for the smartphone industry: build the foundation that everyone else builds on. The company launched Meta Robotics Studio last year, hired former Cruise CEO Marc Whitten to lead the effort, and began recruiting roughly 100 engineers to develop in-house humanoid hardware alongside the AI models that power it. CTO Andrew Bosworth has described humanoid robots as Meta’s next bet of comparable scale to augmented reality, a category in which Meta has already spent tens of billions through its Reality Labs division. The ARI acquisition adds a specific capability to this effort: robot control models that enable humanoids to understand, predict, and adapt to human behaviour in unstructured environments.

The platform strategy is explicit. Meta intends to develop sensors, software, and AI models for robots and make them available to the rest of the industry, meaning the technology could be used by manufacturers that Meta does not own or control. This is the Android model applied to physical
